title: Chocolate Chip Cookies - Claire Saffitz
description: A chewy-edged, soft-centered chocolate chip cookie with puddles of dark and milk chocolate, plenty of salt, and butterscotch-y flavor from vanilla, brown sugar, and brown butter. No stand mixer required.
notes: Chilling the dough is crucial: age for at least 12 hours and up to 48 hours in the fridge before baking. Even 2-4 hours will help. This process allows the butter to solidify, sugar to recrystallize, and flavors to develop, resulting in a chewier cookie with more developed flavor. If using Morton kosher salt instead of Diamond Crystal, use only 1 teaspoon (Morton is saltier). You can use chocolate chips instead of disks, but disks melt into sheets of chocolate which is preferred. Heavy cream can be substituted with half-and-half or whole milk. Brown the butter carefully on low heat to prevent burning—it should be a shade or two past golden brown, not black. Use high-quality vanilla extract, not imitation.

ingredients.name: unsalted butter, cut into tablespoons
ingredients.raw: 2 sticks unsalted butter (8 oz / 227g), cut into tablespoons

ingredients.name: heavy cream, half-and-half, or whole milk
ingredients.raw: 2 tablespoons heavy cream, half-and-half, or whole milk (1 oz / 28g)

ingredients.name: Diamond Crystal kosher salt
ingredients.raw: 2 teaspoons Diamond Crystal kosher salt (0.22 oz / 6g)

ingredients.name: packed dark brown sugar
ingredients.raw: 3/4 cup packed dark brown sugar (5.3 oz / 150g)

ingredients.name: large eggs, cold from the refrigerator
ingredients.raw: 2 large eggs (3.5 oz / 100g), cold from the refrigerator

ingredients.name: bittersweet chocolate disks, half coarsely chopped
ingredients.raw: 5 ounces (142g) bittersweet chocolate disks, half coarsely chopped

ingredients.name: milk chocolate disks, half coarsely chopped
ingredients.raw: 5 ounces (142g) milk chocolate disks, half coarsely chopped

steps.text: Brown {i1} in a saucepan over low to medium-low heat, stirring constantly with a heat-proof spatula to prevent {i2} solids from sticking and burning. Continue cooking until the butter is a shade or two past golden brown (not black). Turn off heat.
Add {i2} to the browned butter and stir to combine. Transfer mixture to a metal bowl and place in an ice bath, stirring constantly until completely cooled and homogeneous.
Add {i6} and {i7} to the cooled butter mixture. Whisk until smooth and homogeneous (no need to cream until light and fluffy).
Add {i8} one at a time, whisking well after each addition until the mixture is silky and smooth.
In a separate bowl, whisk together {i3}, {i5}, and {i4}.
Chop half of {i10} and half of {i11} coarsely, leaving the other half of each as whole disks. Reserve the chocolate dust from chopping.
Add the dry ingredients to the wet ingredients and whisk or fold with a spatula until just combined.
Fold in all the chocolate (chopped and whole pieces, plus any chocolate dust) until evenly distributed.
Using a 2-ounce scoop or 1/4 cup measure, portion the dough into level scoops and place on a baking sheet (they can be close together since they're not baking yet).
Cover and refrigerate the portioned dough for at least 12 hours and up to 48 hours before baking. (Even 2-4 hours will help if you can't wait the full time.)
When ready to bake, preheat oven and prepare baking sheets. Space chilled dough portions appropriately on prepared pans and bake until edges are crispy and centers are soft and chewy.
